chunks: And our companions and others have narrated:

that the Mutamatti' (one who performs Umrah then Hajj), if he misses the Umrah of al-Mut'ah, performs Umah after Hajj, which is what the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) commanded Aisha to do.
And Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Allah has made a way out for the people in that.'

And he (peace be upon him) said: 'The Mutamatti', if he misses the Umrah of al-Mut'ah, remains until the new moon of Muharram, performs Umrah, and it suffices for him in place of the Umrah of al-Mut'ah.'
So when the Mu'tamir finishes his Tawaf and Sa'i, if he wishes he shortens (his hair) and if he wishes he shaves (completely), and shaving is superior.

key_terms.الْمُتَمَتِّعُ: One who performs Umrah al-Mut'ah followed by Hajj
key_terms.عُمْرَةُ الْمُتْعَةِ: The Umrah performed at the beginning of Hajj al-Tamattu'
key_terms.هِلَالُ الْمُحَرَّمِ: The new moon of the month of Muharram

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a Mutamatti' who misses the Umrah of al-Mut'ah before Hajg?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of Hajj al-Tamattu' for those who fail to perform the initial Umrah, establishing that delaying it until the new moon of Muharram is a valid concession (furaj) granted by the Imam. It links this ruling to the precedent of the Prophet commanding Aisha to perform Umrah after Hajj, thereby validating the flexibility in the sequence of rituals. The text concludes with the specific Sunnah of exiting Ihram, noting that shaving the head is superior to shortening the hair.
